paper.title: Context-Aware Proactive Content Caching With Service Differentiation in Wireless Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Context-aware proactive caching (contextual multi-armed bandit, select m of |F| files per slot)
unmapped: Multiple context arrivals per round (U_t <= U_max users, each with a context in [0,1]^D); reward of a file is the sum over users of weighted demands
Expected demand mu_f(x) is Hölder continuous in the context (|mu_f(x)-mu_f(y)| <= L||x-y||^alpha)
Known service-type weights v_s >= 1 and file prioritization weights w_f >= 1 in the reward
Learner knows the context dimension D
settings.definition_quote: The number of times a user with context vector $x\in \mathcal{X}$ requests a file $f\in F$ within one time slot is a random variable with unknown distribution. ... The random demand is assumed to take values in $[0,R_{\max}]$ ... In time slot $t$, the random variables $(d_f(x_{t,i}))_{i=1,..,U_t, f\in F}$, are assumed to be independent ... each random variable $d_f(x_{t,i})$ is assumed to be independent of past caching decisions and previous demands.

settings.name_in_paper: Rating-based context-aware proactive caching with missing ratings
unmapped: Multiple context arrivals per round with Hölder-continuous expected reward in context
Reward is rating times demand; each user's rating (hence feedback) is revealed only with probability q
Learner knows the context dimension D
settings.definition_quote: Then, we define the random variable $\tilde{d}_f(x) := r_f(x) d_f(x)$ ... Let $q\in (0,1)$ be the probability that a user reveals his rating after requesting a file.

algorithms.name: m-CAC (Context-Aware Proactive Caching with Cache Size m)
m-CACao (Context-Aware Proactive Caching with Area Overlap)

bound.expression_latex: O\left(v_{\max} w_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)

symbols.U_max: maximum number of simultaneously connected users
symbols.R_max: maximum demand per user per slot (demands in [0,R_max])
symbols.n_files: number of files |F| in the library

conditions: Assumption 1: expected demands Hölder continuous in context with constants L>0, exponent alpha (beta_holder)

source.label: Theorem_Regret
source.quote: Let $K(t) = t^{\frac{2\alpha}{3 \alpha + D}} \log (t)$ and $h_T = \ceil{T^{\frac{1}{3\alpha + D}}}$. If m-CAC is run with these parameters and Assumption \ref{Ass_Hoelder} holds true, the leading order of the regret $R(T)$ is $O\left(v_{\max} w_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected demands vs per-slot oracle given contexts, so pseudo-regret against best action per round. Paper's alpha (Hölder exponent) mapped to beta_holder; paper's D (context dim) renamed D_ctx. Contexts arbitrary (not modelled as stochastic). Text also states an O(v_max w_max r_max m U_max R_max |F| T^{...} log T) bound for rating-based caching with all ratings revealed (not a separate theorem). Proof only in online appendix.

bound.expression_latex: O\left(\frac{1}{q} v_{\max} w_{\max} r_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)

symbols.q: probability a user reveals a rating
symbols.U_max: maximum number of simultaneously connected users
symbols.R_max: maximum demand per user per slot

conditions: Assumption 1 (Hölder continuity) holds for tilde d_f(x) = r_f(x) d_f(x)
ratings in [r_min, r_max] subset of R_+
rating revealed with probability q in (0,1)

source.label: Theorem_Regret_Rating
source.quote: Let $K(t) = t^{\frac{2\alpha}{3 \alpha + D}} \log (t)$ and $h_T = \ceil{T^{\frac{1}{3\alpha + D}}}$. If m-CAC is run with these parameters with respect to $\tilde{d}_f(x)$, Assumption \ref{Ass_Hoelder} holds true for $\tilde{d}_f(x)$ and a user reveals his rating with probability $q$, the leading order of the regret $R(T)$ is $O\left(\frac{1}{q} v_{\max} w_{\max} r_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)$.

results.notes: Same mapping as Theorem 1; feedback is semi-bandit only when a rating is revealed.
